key_insight: In thin 316L foil laser welding, keyhole instability can nucleate holes that rapidly grow when line energy exceeds the stable seam regime, with growth becoming unstable once hole size approaches sheet thickness.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical stability criterion and precursor signatures to help prevent perforation or cutting in laser welding of ultra-thin sheets.
method: High-speed imaging of laser keyhole welding in 100 μm thin sheets (modeled with 200 μm bead-on-plate foils)
Mapped the sequence from keyhole instability to hole nucleation and growth as line energy increased
Used a Young-Laplace-based force balance to relate curvature-driven surface-tension forces to hole stability
evidence_signal: Continuous weld seams were obtained up to about 7 kJ/m, hole formation appeared above this range, and cutting dominated above about 12 kJ/m, with holes expanding at roughly 0.8–1.2 m/s over 1–3 ms.
watch_item: The stability criterion is derived from a specific thin-sheet geometry and material system, so direct thresholds may shift with alloy, thickness, and laser settings.
paper_title: Rupture and growth of holes in the melt pool during laser keyhole welding of thin sheets
